items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I believe I met Benny last but perhaps heard him perform first.

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Toronto for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m extremely pleased to have Phil Schaap with me here. I’m just going to call you a keeper of the jazz flame, and we can talk about the things you’ve done. You were just talking about, before the cameras were rolling, your teachers. And you mentioned Basie alumnus.

Yeah, well alumni actually, Jo Jones, who the only people who called him Papa Jo Jones when I met him were his children, and some of them were pretty young. A couple of them were not born yet. And he was significantly younger than I am now. I am 51 and he was 44. That’s significant. And Earle Warren, the leader of the reeds. I mean I don’t know whether it was coincidence or because of their camaraderie, which once I intersected with it facilitated more Basieites being involved with the nurturing of me as a child…
